einzeiler: How Trump's foreign policy and trade threats are backfiring and pushing Canada away.
kurzfassung: Canada's former Deputy Prime Minister discusses how Donald Trump's aggressive trade policies and threats to Canadian sovereignty are alienating America's closest ally. Instead of forcing concessions, the pressure has united Canadians and pushed them to diversify trade ties toward Europe and China. Furthermore, she warns that this transactional, dominance-based approach undermines long-standing alliances and ultimately strengthens China's global position.
stichpunkte: Public opinion in Canada has shifted dramatically, with a large percentage now viewing the U.S. with deep concern rather than as a reliable ally.
Donald Trump's aggressive tariffs and rhetoric regarding Canadian sovereignty have united Canadians across political lines to defend their independence.
Canada's strategy during trade disputes focuses on imposing counter-tariffs on politically sensitive U.S. goods to maximize pressure without harming its own economy.
The Trump administration's transactional approach misjudges human and national psychology, driving allies to build defenses and seek alternative partnerships.
China benefits significantly from these tensions, positioning itself as a predictable counterparty while Western alliances fracture.
American business leaders and plutocrats face a dangerous illusion in thinking they can control Trump, mirroring post-Soviet oligarch dynamics.
A growing number of CEOs and business figures are quietly or openly growing alarmed by the economic and security consequences of the current administration's policies.

clips.text: Polling data demonstrates a stark reversal from recent years, as citizens of the northern neighbor now view the superpower as an adversary rather than a partner due to ongoing sovereignty disputes and economic penalties.

clips.hook: Aluminum is electricity in solid form
clips.text: The energy embedded in the aluminum normally shipped across the border equals the output of multiple massive power generation facilities and hundreds of digital infrastructure hubs.

When lawmakers complained that targeted tariffs on locally manufactured goods were hurting their voters, trade negotiators deliberately confirmed that causing localized political friction was the primary objective.

clips.hook: The U.S. perceived as a greater threat than China
clips.text: Survey results across numerous nations reveal that populations in historically friendly democratic states now perceive the leading Western power more negatively than an authoritarian rival.
Highly educated and wealthy individuals in a post-Soviet nation initially backed a leader believing they could easily manipulate him, only to discover that state power ultimately subjugated them.

beschreibung:
If you want to understand the ruins of President Trump’s foreign policy, look no further than Canada. Trump tried to strong-arm America’s trading partner and closest ally with punishing tariffs and threats of becoming the “51st state” in order to extract more concessions.
The result? A recent poll found that 41 percent of Canadians now consider the United States an enemy country. Prime Minister Mark Carney is pursuing closer trade ties with China and Europe in order to diversify away from the U.S. And in August, he walked away from trade talks with the Trump administration, barreling our two countries toward a Jan. 1 deadline when huge new tariffs will go into effect.
Trump’s theory of power appears to have failed here because Canada — even though it’s the weaker party — simply refused to capitulate. There’s a broader lesson in that.
Chrystia Freeland served in a number of senior roles in the Canadian government, including deputy prime minister, minister of finance, and minister of foreign affairs, where she was a lead negotiator for Canada in trade talks with the first Trump administration. She’s the author of a new book, “Unreliable Boyfriend: An Insider’s View of Dealing With a Chaotic Superpower, Plutocrats, and Other Complicated People.”

“How Democrats Drove Silicon Valley Into Trump’s Arms" by Interesting Times

Book Recommendations:
